exhibits.title: The Loom of Similarity
exhibits.text: A loom that measures how nearly two threads run in the same direction. Its shuttle is the DOT PRODUCT: u·v = Σ uᵢvᵢ — multiply matching components, then sum. Geometry gives the number its meaning: u·v = |u|·|v|·cos(θ), the two lengths times the cosine of the angle between the arrows. Large and positive when they point together, zero at a right angle, negative when they oppose — one scalar answering 'how similar are these two?'. The dial enacts it without pause: gold holds still, blue sweeps, and the bar beneath IS u·v, alive — long and warm together, gone at 90°, cold when opposed.

exhibits.title: The Dot Product
exhibits.text: u·v = u₁v₁ + u₂v₂ + … + u_dv_d. Worked: u = [1, 2], v = [3, 1] gives 1·3 + 2·1 = 5. Two readings of that one number: how much of one arrow lies along the other, and |u|·|v|·cos(θ). Cost: d multiplies and adds — nothing more. One habit to file away: raw dot products grow with dimension d (more terms in the sum), so wherever they are compared across sizes you will see them divided by √d to hold a steady scale. Plain bookkeeping — and it explains a coefficient waiting for you upstairs.

exhibits.title: Softmax — Scores into Weights
exhibits.text: Turn raw scores — any real numbers, some negative — into WEIGHTS: all positive, summing to 1. Softmax: weight_i = e^(s_i) / Σ_j e^(s_j). Example: scores [2, 1, 0] → e² , e¹ , e⁰ = 7.39, 2.72, 1.00; divide by their sum 11.11 → [0.66, 0.24, 0.09]. The largest score claims the most weight, but none is silenced. TEMPERATURE divides every score first: large and the weights flatten toward equal, small and they spike toward a single winner. The bars above race forever — their heights are a live softmax.

exhibits.title: From Scores to a Blend
exhibits.spec:
graph LR
  U[vector u] --> D[dot product u·v]
  V[vector v] --> D
  D --> S[score = alignment]
  S --> SM[softmax → weights sum to 1]
  SM --> W[weighted blend of items]
exhibits.caption: Dot product scores alignment; softmax turns a row of scores into positive weights that blend things in proportion.

exhibits.title: From Alignment to Weights
exhibits.caption: Left: the dot product as geometry — a fixed arrow u and partners v at different angles. Nearly aligned → large positive; near a right angle → toward zero; past 90° → negative. Right: a row of raw scores softmaxed into positive weights that sum to 1 — the largest claims the most, none is silenced. Bottom: the same scores with the temperature knob turned — small sharpens toward one winner, large flattens toward equal shares.

exhibits.title: Where This Leads ↑
exhibits.text: Dot product + softmax together are the engine of ATTENTION, one floor up. There the two vectors are renamed QUERY and KEY, and their dot product is one token's relevance to another; every query against every key forms the (n, n) matrix QKᵀ. The √d division you met here is exactly attention's 'scaled' step. And softmax is attention's second half: each row of scores becomes weights that blend the values. The matrix above sweeps row by row — that is attention reading a sentence.
